finding.expected: Preserve the same stable dispatch identity across TASK-062 synchronized self-restart so the restarted canonical code continues the same `aios wakeup` request, invokes at most one PRIMARY, and binds the exact admitted RUN to the existing durable dispatch. Add a deterministic regression covering a wakeup whose preflight actually requires restart and proving the synchronized child retains dispatch identity, produces at most one canonical PRIMARY, and leaves the original dispatch correctly attributable. Preserve direct `aios run`, TASK-071 remote RUN namespace/recover-primary behavior, TASK-072 publication behavior, and all no-retry/no-fallback/no-second-RUN boundaries.
finding.issue: The new `aios wakeup` path durably creates the outer dispatch record before TASK-062 PRIMARY pre-admission synchronization, but when that synchronization fast-forwards to newer canonical code and requires a self-restart, wakeup supplies `_preflight_primary_sync()` with `primary_argv` beginning with `run` rather than preserving the original `wakeup <dispatch_id> ...` command. The synchronized child therefore executes a normal PRIMARY with no dispatch_id and can create a canonical RESULT that is not bound to the durable dispatch. The parent receives only the child's exit code, so a successful child can leave the dispatch without exact RUN ownership and finalize as RECONCILIATION_BLOCKED. Re-delivery is then correctly prohibited from starting another PRIMARY, leaving an otherwise successful remote wakeup permanently unattributed. This violates at-most-once durable ownership across the existing TASK-062 synchronization boundary and also breaks restart/reconciliation guarantees that depend on exact admitted RUN ownership.
